text: The first Olympic Games of the modern era were held in which city in 1896?
explanation: The first Games of the Olympiad of the modern era were celebrated in Athens in 1896.

text: On which date was the International Olympic Committee constituted at the Paris Congress?
explanation: The IOC constituted itself on 23 June 1894 during the Paris Congress associated with the revival of the Olympic Games.

text: Under the Olympic Charter, an Olympiad is a period of how many consecutive calendar years?
options: Two years beginning with the Winter Games
Three years beginning after each Summer Games
Five years beginning with the host selection
explanation: The Charter defines an Olympiad as four consecutive calendar years, beginning on 1 January of the first year.

text: A question asks how Olympic Winter Games are numbered. Which rule gives the correct answer?
options: They are numbered consecutively in the order in which they are held
They are numbered by the four-year Olympiad in which they occur
They restart their numbering whenever a host continent changes
They use the same consecutive numbers as the Summer Games
explanation: Unlike the Games of the Olympiad, Olympic Winter Games are numbered consecutively according to the order in which they are held.

text: In the Olympic symbol, the five interlaced rings primarily represent which idea?
options: Union of continents and athlete meeting
Five sports in the first modern Games
explanation: The Olympic symbol expresses the union of the five continents and the meeting of athletes from throughout the world.

text: Which wording completes the current Olympic motto? “Faster, Higher, Stronger —”
explanation: The current Olympic motto is “Faster, Higher, Stronger — Together”, adding Together to the traditional three-word motto.

text: Which city is scheduled to host the 2028 Summer Olympic Games?
explanation: Los Angeles is the elected host of the 2028 Summer Olympic Games. Brisbane is scheduled for 2032.

text: According to the Olympic Charter, who owns the Olympic Games and the associated Olympic properties?
options: The organising committee of the host city
The National Olympic Committee of Greece
explanation: The Charter states that the Olympic Games are the exclusive property of the IOC, including rights relating to their organisation, broadcasting and use of Olympic properties.

text: Paris 2024 was which numbered Summer Olympic hosting occasion for Paris?
options: The first occasion since the modern Games began
explanation: Paris hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1900, 1924 and again in 2024, making 2024 its third hosting occasion.

text: The 2026 Olympic Winter Games were held under which official host designation?
explanation: The 2026 Olympic Winter Games were the Milano–Cortina Games in Italy.

text: Who became India's first individual Olympic gold medallist?
explanation: Abhinav Bindra became India's first individual Olympic gold medallist by winning the men's 10-metre air rifle at Beijing 2008.

text: In which event did Abhinav Bindra win India's first individual Olympic gold medal?
explanation: Bindra won the men's 10 m air rifle gold at the Beijing 2008 Olympic Games.

text: Who won India's first Olympic gold medal in track and field?
explanation: Neeraj Chopra won India's first Olympic track-and-field gold in the men's javelin at Tokyo 2020, held in 2021.

text: Neeraj Chopra won India's first Olympic track-and-field gold in which event?
explanation: Chopra won the men's javelin throw at the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games.

text: How many medals did India win at the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games?
explanation: India won seven medals at Tokyo 2020: one gold, two silver and four bronze medals.

text: How many medals did India win at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games?
explanation: India's Paris 2024 tally was six medals: one silver and five bronze medals.

text: Which description correctly states India's Paris 2024 Olympic medal composition?
options: One gold, two silver and three bronze medals
Two silver and four bronze medals
One silver and five bronze medals
Two gold and four bronze medals
explanation: India won one silver medal and five bronze medals at Paris 2024, with no gold medal in the tally.

text: What medal did Neeraj Chopra win in the men's javelin at Paris 2024?
explanation: Neeraj Chopra won the silver medal in the men's javelin at Paris 2024; Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem won gold.

text: What notable Paris 2024 achievement did Manu Bhaker record for India?
options: First Indian woman with two Olympic medals
explanation: Manu Bhaker won two bronze medals at Paris 2024: in the women's 10 m air pistol and the mixed 10 m air pistol team event.

text: Which result did the Indian men's hockey team achieve at Paris 2024?
explanation: India won the men's hockey bronze medal at Paris 2024 by defeating Spain, successfully defending the bronze won at Tokyo 2020.

text: Which city hosted the inaugural Asian Games in 1951?
explanation: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, from 4 to 11 March 1951.

text: The first Asian Games were held in which year?
explanation: The inaugural Asian Games took place in New Delhi in 1951. The Asian Games Federation had been formed earlier, in 1949.

text: How many National Olympic Committees participated in the inaugural New Delhi 1951 Asian Games?
explanation: The official OCA record for New Delhi 1951 lists 11 participating NOCs.

text: Which statement about New Delhi 1982 is correct?
options: It was India's first Asian Games and the first under the OCA
It was the first Asian Games held outside Asia
It was the first edition to be held in two countries
It was the second Asian Games hosted by Delhi
explanation: New Delhi 1982 was the ninth Asian Games and the second edition hosted by Delhi, after the inaugural 1951 Games.

text: New Delhi 1982 was historically significant because it was the first Asian Games held under which organisation?
explanation: The 1982 Delhi Asian Games were the first held under the aegis of the Olympic Council of Asia; the first eight had been under the Asian Games Federation.

text: After the inaugural edition, the Asian Games were generally organised at what interval?
explanation: The OCA history records that, from the second Asian Games onward, the Games were organised once every four years, subject to exceptional postponements.

text: The 2018 Asian Games were hosted jointly by which Indonesian cities?
explanation: The 2018 Asian Games were held in Jakarta and Palembang, Indonesia.

text: Which city hosted the 2014 Asian Games?
explanation: The 17th Asian Games were held in Incheon, South Korea, in 2014.

text: Which city hosted the 15th Asian Games in 2006?
explanation: The 15th Asian Games were held in Doha, Qatar, in 2006.

text: The 11th Asian Games in 1990 were held in which city?
explanation: The 11th Asian Games were held in Beijing, China, in 1990.

subtopic: Current Asian Games cycle and Indian performance
text: Why may the most recent Asian Games be described as Hangzhou 2022 even though its competitions took place in 2023?
options: The host moved from Hangzhou to another city
The OCA renumbered the Games after closing
The Games were held twice, once in each year
The event was postponed from 2022 to 2023
explanation: The event retained the Hangzhou 2022 designation but was held from 23 September to 8 October 2023 after postponement. It was the 19th Asian Games.

subtopic: Current Asian Games cycle and Indian performance
text: What was India's total medal tally at the Hangzhou Asian Games?
explanation: India finished fourth at Hangzhou with 107 medals: 28 gold, 38 silver and 41 bronze.

subtopic: Current Asian Games cycle and Indian performance
text: Which medal combination correctly represents India's 107 medals at Hangzhou?
explanation: The official OCA medal table lists India's Hangzhou tally as 28 gold, 38 silver and 41 bronze medals.

subtopic: Current Asian Games cycle and Indian performance
text: Where did India finish in the Hangzhou Asian Games medal standings?
explanation: India ranked fourth in the Hangzhou medal table behind China, Japan and the Republic of Korea.

subtopic: Current Asian Games cycle and Indian performance
text: Aichi–Nagoya 2026 is which numbered edition of the Asian Games?
explanation: Aichi–Nagoya 2026 is the 20th Asian Games, following the 19th Games in Hangzhou.

subtopic: Current Asian Games cycle and Indian performance
text: What are the scheduled dates for the Aichi–Nagoya 2026 Asian Games?
explanation: The OCA lists the 20th Asian Games in Aichi–Nagoya for 19 September to 4 October 2026.

subtopic: Current Asian Games cycle and Indian performance
text: Which city is listed to host the 2030 Asian Games?
explanation: The OCA Games timeline lists Doha as the host city for the 2030 Asian Games and Riyadh for 2034.

subtopic: Current Asian Games cycle and Indian performance
text: Which city is listed to host the 2034 Asian Games?
explanation: The OCA Games timeline lists Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, as the host city for the 2034 Asian Games.

subtopic: Current Asian Games cycle and Indian performance
text: Which statement about India's Hangzhou 2023 performance is accurate?
options: India finished fourth with a record 107 medals, including 28 gold
India finished second with 70 medals, including 16 gold
India finished third with 111 medals, including 28 gold
India finished fifth with 96 medals, including 20 gold
explanation: India finished fourth at Hangzhou with 107 medals, including 28 gold. The 70-medal figure refers to India's 2018 Jakarta–Palembang tally, not Hangzhou.

subtopic: Current Asian Games cycle and Indian performance
text: Which e-sports statement was confirmed by the OCA for Aichi–Nagoya 2026?
options: The OCA removed all e-sports from the programme
Only Olympic sports could enter the programme
India alone selected every team-sport entry
The OCA announced 11 e-sports titles for the Games
explanation: The OCA announced 11 e-sports titles for the 2026 Asian Games; the event itself was scheduled for September–October 2026 as of the coverage date.

text: Which of the following is a component of the revised Khelo India Scheme for 2021–22 to 2025–26?
options: National Sports Science and Research Programme
National Anti-Doping Testing and Education Network
Creation and Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure
explanation: The revised Khelo India Scheme lists Creation and Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure as one of its five components. The other options are not components named in that scheme structure.

text: Which revised Khelo India component brings together sports competitions, talent identification and community coaching development?
options: Fit India Movement and School Fitness
Khelo India Centres and Sports Academies
explanation: The revised scheme groups sports competitions, talent search and development, and community coaching under Sports Competitions and Talent Development.

text: Which set represents the three national-level Khelo India competitions identified in the revised operational guidelines?
options: Youth Games, National Games and Asian Games
Youth Games, University Games and Winter Games
University Games, National Games and Commonwealth Games
Winter Games, Para-Asian Games and Olympic Games
explanation: The revised operational guidelines identify Khelo India Youth Games, Khelo India University Games and Khelo India Winter Games as annual national-level competitions.

text: A Khelo India talent-identification drive is being planned across several states. Which approach best matches the scheme guidelines?
options: Use transparent performance evidence and scientific testing
Select athletes only from previously famous clubs
Use only coach reputation and informal recommendations
Rank athletes only by their social-media following
explanation: The guidelines describe transparent identification using competitive performance and a scientifically designed battery of tests, with wider access through competitions and talent-search mechanisms.

text: Which revised Khelo India component specifically addresses inclusion through sport?
options: Creation and Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure
Khelo India Centres and Sports Academies
explanation: Promotion of Inclusiveness through Sports is one of the five revised components and covers inclusion-oriented sport initiatives, including participation of groups such as persons with disabilities and women.

text: Which organization is identified in official Indian sports material as implementing the Khelo India Scheme?
options: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
explanation: Khelo India is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. SAI supports and operates several sports-promotional activities within the national sports ecosystem.

text: The principal purpose of Khelo India national-level competitions is to provide a platform for which of the following?
explanation: The operational guidelines describe Khelo India Games as a platform to showcase sporting skills, spot talent and provide development pathways for gifted athletes.

text: Which event is listed by SAI among the Khelo India national-level competitions and initiatives?
explanation: SAI's current public information lists Khelo India Youth Games, University Games, Winter Games and Para Games among the national-level Khelo India competitions and initiatives.

text: A district has athletes but lacks a safe, usable training venue. Which Khelo India component most directly addresses this gap?
options: Fit India Movement and School Fitness Activities
explanation: A shortage of usable training facilities is an infrastructure gap, so Creation and Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure is the most direct component for the proposed intervention.

text: A state wants to develop continuing local training access around existing facilities and academies. Which Khelo India component is the closest fit?
options: Fit India Movement for School Fitness
Khelo India Centres and Sports Academies
Creation and Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure
explanation: Khelo India Centres and Sports Academies is the component most directly linked with local training structures and academy support, whereas infrastructure creation alone does not describe the continuing training pathway.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: In which year did the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports start the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)?
explanation: Official Ministry and SAI material states that MYAS started TOPS in September 2014 to improve India's performance at the Olympics and Paralympics.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: TOPS was revamped to establish a technical support team for managing athletes in which year and month?
explanation: The SAI and MYAS description records that TOPS was revamped in April 2018 to establish a technical support team and provide holistic support to TOPS athletes.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: Which organization currently handles the Target Olympic Podium Scheme according to the official sports-portal description?
explanation: The Ministry's National Sports Development Fund page states that the TOP Scheme is now handled by the Sports Authority of India, with grants provided from NSDF.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: Which body approves customized programmes for athletes selected under TOPS?
explanation: The Mission Olympic Cell is described as approving customized programmes for TOPS athletes and recommending financial disbursement for those programmes.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: A TOPS athlete submits a proposal for overseas training. Which activity falls within the Mission Olympic Cell's stated responsibilities?
options: Issuing the athlete's passport for overseas training
Replacing the athlete's federation in competition
Evaluating proposals and reviewing athlete progress
explanation: The official TOPS description assigns the Mission Olympic Cell responsibility for evaluating proposals and periodically reviewing athletes' progress and performance; it does not replace other institutions.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: What is the principal benchmark described for selecting athletes under TOPS?
options: Popularity in domestic media coverage alone
Number of years in a state academy alone
explanation: Official TOPS information states that selection benchmarks relate to international standards and consistency in performance, with research and consultation also informing identification.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: Which fund provides grants for TOPS-related training, travel and equipment requirements?
explanation: The official NSDF description states that grants from the National Sports Development Fund are placed at SAI's disposal to meet training, travel and equipment requirements of athletes selected in TOPS.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: Which package best represents the type of support that TOPS can provide to a selected elite athlete?
options: Only a domestic participation certificate and medal
Only a rule change and transfer to another sport
Customized training, exposure and equipment support
Only a general physical-education textbook and lecture
explanation: TOPS is intended to provide personalized support, including customized training, foreign or international exposure, equipment and coaching-camp support for selected athletes.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: An athlete has an excellent past reputation but inconsistent recent performances. Which selection approach is most consistent with TOPS criteria?
options: Select automatically because past reputation is sufficient
Reject automatically because only current ranking matters
Review current form, consistency, fitness and benchmarks
Select only after a public vote by national spectators
explanation: TOPS identification considers performance against international standards, current performance, consistency and fitness through research and consultation; past reputation alone is not the stated benchmark.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: What is the best description of the Core and Development groups used within TOPS?
options: Support groups for medal prospects and developing athletes
Two groups separating event officials from spectators
Two groups classifying venues by construction cost
Two groups applying only to anti-doping laboratory work
explanation: TOPS uses Core and Development group pathways to support leading medal prospects and promising athletes at a developmental stage; both are athlete-support categories within the scheme.

text: In which year was the Sports Authority of India established?
explanation: SAI was set up in 1984 as a successor to the legacy of the IX Asian Games held in New Delhi in 1982.

text: Which pair best describes the broad objectives entrusted to SAI?
options: Conducting examinations and licensing private gyms
Running professional sports leagues and ticket sales
Promoting sports and achieving sporting excellence
Regulating international federations and Olympic rules
explanation: SAI's official description gives it the twin objectives of promoting sports and achieving sporting excellence at national and international levels.

text: What is the principal purpose of a SAI National Centre of Excellence (NCOE)?
options: To replace all district sports associations
To provide only short-term recreational activities
To conduct only anti-doping adjudication hearings
To provide specialized training to promising athletes
explanation: SAI describes NCOEs as centres that train promising athletes for excellence in the Olympics and other international events through specialized training and high-performance support.

text: Which combination is specifically described as part of the support available at SAI NCOEs?
options: Only stadium ticketing, advertising and event-broadcasting services
Only academic examinations and non-sport hostel administration
Sports-science backup, individualized diet and staff supervision
Only selection trials without coaching or medical support
explanation: The NCOE description includes state-of-the-art facilities, sports-science backup, individualized diets prescribed by trained nutritionists, and supervision by coaches and qualified support staff.

text: Which abbreviation denotes the SAI Training Centre scheme?
explanation: STC stands for SAI Training Centre. SAI lists STC alongside NCOE, Extension Centres and NSTC among its sports-promotional schemes.

text: Which set of sub-schemes is associated with the National Sports Talent Contest (NSTC) in SAI's scheme description?
options: Olympic cities, World Cups and Asian Games
Regular Schools, IGMA Schools and Akharas
explanation: SAI's scheme description lists NSTC with sub-schemes for Regular Schools and Indigenous Games & Martial Arts (IGMA) Schools and Akharas.

text: An identified athlete needs residential high-performance training, sports-science support and an individualized nutrition plan. Which SAI setting is the closest match?
explanation: NCOEs are designed for specialized high-performance training and provide sports-science backup, individualized diet and overall supervision for promising athletes.

text: Which activity is explicitly included among SAI's key functions?
options: Writing the rules of every sport
explanation: SAI's current official overview identifies talent identification and development as one of its key functions, along with infrastructure, inclusivity, high-performance training and sports-science support.

text: A national training centre asks which SAI function covers specialist clinical care and rehabilitation support for athletes. Which answer is most appropriate?
explanation: SAI's organisational information identifies Sports Medicine and Medical Support as a function providing comprehensive medical care, including specialist services and rehabilitation.

text: What does the abbreviation NSRS represent in SAI's athlete-support ecosystem?
explanation: NSRS stands for National Sports Repository System. SAI's organisational information lists development and maintenance of NSRS among its digital-platform functions.

text: Which body describes itself as the governing body for the Olympic Movement and the Commonwealth Games in India?
options: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
explanation: The Indian Olympic Association states that it is the governing body for the Olympic Movement and the Commonwealth Games in India and administers related governance and athlete-welfare matters.

text: Which responsibility is assigned to the Indian Olympic Association in its official organisational description?
options: Overseeing Indian teams at Olympic, Asian and multi-sport events
Running each National Sports Federation's daily coaching programme
Administering all prohibited-substance laboratory analyses nationwide
Building every SAI training centre without state participation
explanation: The IOA describes overseeing representation of Indian athletes and teams at the Olympic Games, Commonwealth Games, Asian Games and other relevant international multi-sport competitions as part of its role.

text: A Khelo India competition is being organised in a recognised Olympic sport. Which partner should be associated for sport-specific technical coordination under the guidelines?
options: A foreign embassy without a sport body
explanation: The Khelo India operational guidelines state that the concerned National Sports Federations are associated with Khelo India national-level competitions, alongside relevant school, university or winter-sport bodies.

text: Which ministry owns the Khelo India – National Programme for Development of Sports as a Central Sector Scheme?
options: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
explanation: The official scheme description identifies the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports as the ministry implementing the Khelo India – National Programme for Development of Sports.

text: Which authority publishes the official list of recognised National Sports Federations in India?
options: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
explanation: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports maintains and publishes official recognition information for National Sports Federations, including the ministry's recognised-federation list.

text: For a sport-specific national team, which body normally leads the technical selection and training of competitors, while the IOA handles broader multi-sport representation?
explanation: The IOA's historical and organisational material distinguishes its multi-sport representation role from the sport-specific work of National Sports Federations, which select and train competitors in their sport.

text: The National Sports Development Code of India is primarily associated with governance and compliance of which national sports bodies?
options: Only private fitness clubs and gyms
explanation: Official MYAS materials identify the National Sports Development Code as applying to governance matters involving the IOA and National Sports Federations, including transparency and compliance expectations.

text: The Indian Olympic Association identifies affiliation with which set of international bodies?
options: WADA, NADA, FIFA and ICC sports bodies
UNESCO, WHO, UNICEF and UNDP agencies
IOC, CGF, OCA and ANOC Olympic bodies
FIBA, World Athletics, ITF and UCI bodies
explanation: The IOA organisational page identifies it as affiliated with the International Olympic Committee, Commonwealth Games Federation, Olympic Council of Asia and Association of National Olympic Committees.

text: An Indian delegation is being prepared for a multi-sport event involving several National Sports Federations. Which body coordinates India's broader representation in that event?
options: The federation of only the largest participating sport
Indian Olympic Association for national representation
The event's ticketing and hospitality contractor
A district sports association with no national role
explanation: The IOA states that it oversees the representation of Indian athletes and teams at major international multi-sport competitions, while sport-specific federations retain technical roles.

text: Which arrangement best reflects the coordination model for a Khelo India national competition?
options: A single private sponsor conducts the event without a sport federation
The relevant NSF works with state, school, university and winter bodies
The IOA replaces all local organisers and provides every coach
The anti-doping authority selects athletes and manages schedules
explanation: The Khelo India guidelines describe association with the concerned NSFs and relevant school, university and winter-sport bodies, rather than a single-body or anti-doping-led model.

text: Under Article 2.1 of the 2021 World Anti-Doping Code, which circumstance constitutes an anti-doping rule violation?
options: Presence of a prohibited substance or its marker in an athlete’s sample
Failure to meet a planned training load during an out-of-competition week
Use of a documented medicine recorded only in a team’s internal file
A performance result below the athlete’s previous season best
explanation: Article 2.1 addresses the presence of a prohibited substance, its metabolites or markers in an athlete’s sample. The rule is not based on performance level or training load.

text: The strict-liability principle in the WADA Code means that, for an Article 2.1 violation, which fact need not be proved by the anti-doping organization?
options: The identity of the athlete who provided the sample
The presence of a prohibited substance, metabolite or marker
The validity of the laboratory’s analytical report
Intent, fault, negligence or knowing use by the athlete
explanation: For presence in a sample under Article 2.1, the athlete’s personal responsibility applies without requiring proof of intent, fault, negligence or knowing use. Fault can still affect consequences.

text: Which conduct is addressed by Article 2.2 of the 2021 World Anti-Doping Code?
options: Use or attempted use of a prohibited substance or method
Failure to update a quarterly whereabouts filing on time
Possession of a prohibited substance by support staff
Association with an ineligible support person at work
explanation: Article 2.2 concerns the use or attempted use of a prohibited substance or prohibited method by an athlete. It is distinct from presence, whereabouts and association violations.

text: A staff member deliberately alters a doping-control document to conceal a medication. Which Code concept best describes this conduct?
options: Tampering or attempted tampering with doping control
A filing failure under the whereabouts requirements
A protected-person classification under the Code
An atypical finding requiring routine laboratory review
explanation: Intentionally subverting the doping-control process, including falsifying documents, falls within tampering or attempted tampering under Article 2.5.

text: Under Article 2.10, which relationship may constitute a prohibited-association violation?
options: A professional clinical relationship for ordinary care
A professional relationship with a person serving a ban
A social meeting with a retired athlete outside sport
A medical referral before entering a testing pool
explanation: Article 2.10 concerns certain prohibited association with an athlete-support person who is serving ineligibility or has been convicted or professionally sanctioned for conduct equivalent to a Code violation. A normal consultation or casual contact alone is not the rule’s target.

text: A coach threatens an athlete after the athlete makes a good-faith report of suspected doping. Which response is most consistent with Article 2.11?
options: Treat the threat as a private team-management disagreement
Recognize possible retaliation against anti-doping reporting
Wait for a positive laboratory result before recording the conduct
Classify the threat as a missed test because it affects availability
explanation: Article 2.11 addresses discouraging or retaliating against a person who reports information in good faith. A positive test is not required for the reporting-related conduct to be relevant.

text: What is a central purpose of the World Anti-Doping Code?
options: To harmonize anti-doping rules across sports and countries
To replace the medical judgment of every team physician
To limit testing to athletes competing at Olympic Games
To let each federation define prohibited substances independently
explanation: The Code provides a common framework intended to harmonize anti-doping rules, responsibilities and procedures across sports and jurisdictions.

text: According to WADA’s clean-sport education approach, who has responsibility for learning and following anti-doping rules?
options: Only the laboratory that analyzes the sample
Athletes, support personnel and anti-doping organizations
Only the national federation’s legal department
Only athletes who have already received a positive result
explanation: WADA describes education as everyone’s responsibility. Athletes and support personnel must seek information and comply, while anti-doping organizations must provide appropriate education.

text: In a doping hearing, which standard must the anti-doping organization generally satisfy under Article 3.1?
options: Proof beyond any possible scientific doubt
A simple assertion by the treating clinician
Comfortable satisfaction of the hearing panel
A unanimous decision by every testing laboratory
explanation: Article 3.1 uses the hearing panel’s comfortable satisfaction, a standard greater than a mere balance of probability but less than proof beyond reasonable doubt.

text: A team doctor knowingly gives an athlete a prohibited substance without a valid therapeutic authorization. Which Code violation is most directly implicated?
options: Failure to declare a daily training location
Administration of a prohibited substance or method
Presence of a marker in a biological passport only
Prohibited association with a retired athlete
explanation: Article 2.8 addresses administration or attempted administration of a prohibited substance or method. A support person’s conduct can therefore be an anti-doping rule violation even apart from the athlete’s sample result.

subtopic: Prohibited List and therapeutic use exemptions
text: As of 2026-08-16, when did the WADA 2026 Prohibited List take effect?
explanation: WADA states that the 2026 List of Prohibited Substances and Methods came into effect on 1 January 2026. The date in this question is the bank’s current verification date.

subtopic: Prohibited List and therapeutic use exemptions
text: Which category in the 2026 WADA Prohibited List contains anabolic agents?
explanation: S1 is the Prohibited List category for anabolic agents. S3 covers beta-2 agonists, S5 diuretics and masking agents, and S9 glucocorticoids.

subtopic: Prohibited List and therapeutic use exemptions
text: Erythropoietin and related erythropoiesis-stimulating agents are listed under which WADA category?
options: S2: Peptide hormones and growth factors
explanation: Erythropoietins and agents affecting erythropoiesis are covered by S2, the category for peptide hormones, growth factors, related substances and mimetics.

subtopic: Prohibited List and therapeutic use exemptions
text: Hydrochlorothiazide and furosemide are examples associated with which 2026 Prohibited List category?
options: S2: peptide hormones and growth factors
explanation: Hydrochlorothiazide and furosemide are diuretics and are listed under S5, diuretics and masking agents, which is prohibited at all times unless an applicable authorization exists.

subtopic: Prohibited List and therapeutic use exemptions
text: Under the 2026 WADA List, systemic injectable, oral or rectal glucocorticoids are classified in which way?
options: S3: beta-2 agonists, with route limits
S5: diuretics and masking agents, at all times
explanation: S9 covers glucocorticoids. The 2026 List prohibits them in-competition when administered by injectable, oral including oromucosal, or rectal routes; route and timing matter.

subtopic: Prohibited List and therapeutic use exemptions
text: Beta-blockers are placed in which part of the WADA List?
options: S1: Anabolic agents, prohibited at all times
M3: Gene doping, prohibited at all times
explanation: Beta-blockers are listed under P1 and are prohibited only in the particular sports specified by the List. They are not a universal S-class prohibition.

subtopic: Prohibited List and therapeutic use exemptions
text: What is the purpose of a Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE)?
options: To authorize medically necessary prohibited treatment under the ISTUE
To remove an athlete from every registered testing pool
To permit any supplement sold by a recognized federation
To replace diagnosis with a coach’s treatment statement
explanation: A TUE permits use of an otherwise prohibited substance or method for a legitimate medical condition when the required criteria and documentation are satisfied. It is not a blanket exemption from testing.

subtopic: Prohibited List and therapeutic use exemptions
text: Which statement reflects one of the criteria considered when granting a TUE?
options: The treatment must improve performance beyond normal health in competition
The treatment should add no performance enhancement beyond normal health
A permitted alternative can always be ignored by the TUE committee
A prescription automatically approves medication for competition
explanation: One ISTUE criterion is that therapeutic use should not produce additional enhancement of performance beyond what is anticipated from returning to normal health. Other criteria, including medical necessity and lack of a reasonable permitted alternative, also apply.

subtopic: Prohibited List and therapeutic use exemptions
text: When evaluating a TUE application, which additional medical consideration is required by the ISTUE framework?
options: The athlete’s sponsor must approve the treatment first
The treatment must be the most expensive available option
The athlete must have used the substance before entering sport
There must be no reasonable permitted therapeutic alternative
explanation: The ISTUE criteria include the absence of a reasonable permitted therapeutic alternative. A sponsor’s preference, price and prior non-sport use do not establish a TUE.

subtopic: Prohibited List and therapeutic use exemptions
text: An athlete receives urgent emergency treatment with a prohibited medicine before a prospective TUE can be obtained. What is the appropriate next step?
options: Assume emergency care automatically removes a violation
Remove the medicine from the medical record
Apply for a retroactive TUE after emergency treatment
Ask the coach to replace the TUE application
explanation: The ISTUE allows defined retroactive applications, including certain emergency circumstances, but approval is not automatic. The athlete and physician must document the treatment and satisfy the applicable criteria.

text: Under Article 2.1.2, when can an athlete’s A sample establish an anti-doping rule violation without analysis of the B sample?
options: A coach confirms the collection was correct and complete
The athlete waives B analysis and A meets Code rules
Both samples are destroyed after the laboratory report
A third athlete provides a matching sample that day
explanation: Article 2.1.2 recognizes the A sample as sufficient when the athlete waives analysis of the B sample and the applicable evidentiary requirements are met. The B sample is otherwise used for confirmation when analyzed.

text: What is the principal role of a Doping Control Officer during a testing session?
options: To decide the athlete’s sanction at the competition venue
To prescribe treatment for declared medication
To ratify the athlete’s performance result
To supervise secure collection and protect athlete rights
explanation: The Doping Control Officer conducts or supervises sample collection according to the applicable testing standard, including identity, documentation, security and the athlete’s procedural rights. Sanctions are decided through results management and adjudication.

text: What information is an athlete in a Registered Testing Pool generally required to provide through whereabouts filings?
options: Only the athlete’s preferred competition venue
Only medicines taken during the previous calendar year
Quarterly whereabouts with a daily one-hour slot and location
A permanent guarantee against international travel
explanation: RTP athletes file whereabouts information for the forthcoming quarter and specify a daily 60-minute slot at a stated location. The filing also includes other information needed to locate the athlete for testing.

text: The daily 60-minute whereabouts slot for an RTP athlete must generally fall within which period?
explanation: The whereabouts rules require a precise 60-minute slot each day between 05:00 and 23:00. This slot does not remove the athlete’s broader obligation to submit to authorized testing.

text: An RTP athlete accumulates three filing failures and/or missed tests within a rolling 12-month period. What is the anti-doping implication?
options: The combination may constitute a whereabouts violation under Article 2.4
It is automatically ignored if the athlete later wins a medal
It is treated only as a laboratory quality-control problem
It becomes a TUE application because no prohibited substance was detected
explanation: Any combination of three whereabouts failures within a 12-month period may constitute an Article 2.4 anti-doping rule violation, subject to the applicable results-management process.

text: An RTP athlete argues that testing is permitted only during the 60-minute slot entered in ADAMS. Which response is correct?
options: Incorrect: the slot defines availability, not all testing
Correct: the slot limits all authorized testing to one hour
Correct: but only in weeks without a competition
Incorrect: testing is permitted only at the listed home address
explanation: The 60-minute slot helps establish availability for a missed-test assessment, but it does not limit the athlete’s obligation to submit to testing at any time and place when an authorized organization requests it.

text: What is ADAMS primarily used for in the anti-doping system?
options: To score technical performance during a competition
To securely manage whereabouts, testing and records
To replace laboratory analysis with coach observations
To issue medals and maintain official event results
explanation: ADAMS is WADA’s secure online system for managing anti-doping information, including whereabouts and testing-related records. It is not a competition-scoring platform.

text: What does an Adverse Analytical Finding generally indicate?
options: The athlete fails to reach a prescribed training intensity
A coach submits an incomplete competition travel itinerary
A TUE committee approves a documented medical treatment
A WADA-accredited lab reports a prohibited marker
explanation: An Adverse Analytical Finding is a laboratory result indicating the presence of a prohibited substance, its metabolites or markers, or evidence of a prohibited method, subject to the applicable review and results-management process.

text: A laboratory reports an atypical result that is not yet an Adverse Analytical Finding. What should happen next?
explanation: An atypical finding signals that further investigation may be needed; it is not by itself an ADRV. The responsible anti-doping organization follows the applicable laboratory and results-management procedures.

text: An athlete waives analysis of the B sample after the A sample reports a prohibited substance. Which statement is correct under Article 2.1.2?
options: The result is treated only as a training error
The laboratory creates a third sample before proceeding
The waiver automatically proves intentional use
A result may establish violation if Code rules are met
explanation: When an athlete waives B-sample analysis, the A-sample result can be sufficient to establish an Article 2.1 violation if the Code’s requirements are met. The waiver does not itself prove intent.

subtopic: Athlete Biological Passport, supplements and education
text: What is the primary purpose of the Athlete Biological Passport (ABP)?
options: Replace all urine and blood tests during a season
Certify supplements as free of prohibited substances
Rank athletes by comparing competition results
Monitor biological variables over time for doping patterns
explanation: The ABP uses longitudinal biological profiles to identify patterns that may indicate manipulation of physiological variables. It supports anti-doping investigations rather than ranking athletes or replacing all testing.

subtopic: Athlete Biological Passport, supplements and education
text: How should the Athlete Biological Passport be understood in relation to conventional analytical testing?
options: It is used only when no biological sample can be collected
It makes the Prohibited List unnecessary for all sports
It complements traditional testing without replacing all analysis
It is a medical treatment record that cannot support investigations
explanation: WADA describes the ABP as a complementary strategy. Longitudinal profiling can guide target testing and investigations, while conventional analytical methods remain part of the anti-doping program.

subtopic: Athlete Biological Passport, supplements and education
text: The hematological module of the ABP is most directly concerned with longitudinal patterns in which type of data?
options: Blood variables linked to oxygen transport
explanation: The hematological module profiles blood-related variables over time and can help identify patterns consistent with blood manipulation or blood-doping practices. It is not a performance-ranking or imaging system.

subtopic: Athlete Biological Passport, supplements and education
text: The steroidal module of the ABP primarily uses longitudinal information about which profile?
options: Daily step counts from a wearable device
explanation: The steroidal module tracks steroid-related variables longitudinally, commonly using repeated urine profiles, to help identify patterns requiring anti-doping follow-up.

subtopic: Athlete Biological Passport, supplements and education
text: What is a suitable description of ADAMS in relation to Athlete Biological Passport programs?
options: A secure system for anti-doping data and reports
A public database of every athlete’s medical record
A replacement for expert review of a profile
explanation: WADA describes ADAMS as a secure online database that supports data entry, storage, sharing and reporting in anti-doping operations, including ABP administration. It does not replace expert review or make medical records public.

subtopic: Athlete Biological Passport, supplements and education
text: Before an international-level athlete competes, which anti-doping preparation is most appropriate?
options: Wait for notification before seeking information
Rely on a supplement company's safety statement
Learn anti-doping rights, List, TUEs and testing
Ask a coach to decide medication status alone
explanation: WADA’s education material emphasizes advance knowledge of rights and responsibilities, the Prohibited List, TUEs and the doping-control process. Preparation should not begin only after a test notification.

subtopic: Athlete Biological Passport, supplements and education
text: What is the safest general anti-doping statement about dietary supplements?
options: A club’s retail channel establishes that a supplement is permitted
The word natural makes a supplement safe for every athlete
Assess the supplement’s quality and contamination risk first
Checking is needed only after an adverse analytical finding
explanation: The AIS position statement emphasizes a risk–reward approach because supplements may be contaminated, inaccurately labeled or unsuitable. Marketing language and retail location do not establish anti-doping safety.

subtopic: Athlete Biological Passport, supplements and education
text: What does credible batch testing of a supplement establish?
options: It proves suitability for every athlete and medical condition
It gives a manufacturer authority to issue a TUE
It removes the athlete’s personal responsibility
It can reduce contamination risk but cannot guarantee safety
explanation: Batch testing and quality controls can reduce, but do not eliminate, contamination and labeling risks. The athlete remains responsible for substances found in the body under the Code.

subtopic: Athlete Biological Passport, supplements and education
text: A product marketed to an athlete contains a proprietary blend and gives no clear assurance about prohibited ingredients. What is the best next step?
options: Use it because proprietary blends are exempt under the rules
Ask a teammate to approve it after one serving and review
Check ingredients and contamination risk with qualified advice
Hide it from the medical team to avoid any record
explanation: An unclear proprietary blend increases uncertainty about composition and contamination. The athlete should obtain qualified advice, verify ingredients and assess whether the potential benefit justifies the anti-doping and health risk.

subtopic: Athlete Biological Passport, supplements and education
text: An athlete-support person knowingly helps an athlete use a prohibited method. Which Code concept most directly applies?
options: A routine whereabouts filing update with no misconduct
A permitted therapeutic intervention without required documentation
Complicity or attempted complicity in an anti-doping violation
An atypical laboratory finding without a conduct violation
explanation: Article 2.9 addresses complicity or attempted complicity, including knowingly assisting, encouraging, aiding, abetting, conspiring or covering up an anti-doping rule violation. Support personnel therefore have direct Code responsibilities.

subtopic: Commonwealth Games history, editions and Indian performance
text: The first Commonwealth Games, held in 1930, took place in which city?
explanation: The inaugural Games were held in Hamilton, Canada, in 1930. They were then known as the British Empire Games.

subtopic: Commonwealth Games history, editions and Indian performance
text: Which organisation directs the Commonwealth Games movement?
explanation: Commonwealth Sport is the organisation responsible for the direction and delivery of the Commonwealth Games movement; it was formerly known as the Commonwealth Games Federation.

subtopic: Commonwealth Games history, editions and Indian performance
text: Which city hosted the 2022 Commonwealth Games?
explanation: The XXII Commonwealth Games were held in Birmingham, England, from 28 July to 8 August 2022.

subtopic: Commonwealth Games history, editions and Indian performance
text: As of 16 August 2026, which city hosted the XXIII Commonwealth Games?
explanation: Glasgow hosted the XXIII Commonwealth Games from 23 July to 2 August 2026 after Victoria withdrew as host. Amdavad is the announced host for 2030.

subtopic: Commonwealth Games history, editions and Indian performance
text: Which city was confirmed as host of the 2030 Commonwealth Games, the centenary edition?
explanation: Commonwealth Sport confirmed Amdavad, India, as host of the 2030 Centenary Games.

subtopic: Commonwealth Games history, editions and Indian performance
text: At Birmingham 2022, which country finished first in the overall medal table?
explanation: Australia topped the Birmingham 2022 medal table with 67 gold medals; Commonwealth Sport's later host announcement records Australia as the leader.

subtopic: Commonwealth Games history, editions and Indian performance
text: The Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games programme was organised around how many sports?
explanation: The official Glasgow 2026 information describes a 10-sport programme, including six fully integrated Para Sports.

subtopic: Commonwealth Games history, editions and Indian performance
text: What was the original name of the Games first held at Hamilton in 1930?
explanation: The first edition in Hamilton in 1930 was called the British Empire Games. The event adopted different names as the Commonwealth movement evolved.

subtopic: Commonwealth Games history, editions and Indian performance
text: On which dates were the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games held?
explanation: Birmingham 2022 ran from 28 July to 8 August 2022. The other dates correspond to different Commonwealth Games editions or hosts.

subtopic: Commonwealth Games history, editions and Indian performance
text: How many nations and territories took part in Glasgow 2026?
explanation: The official Glasgow 2026 event information lists athletes from 74 nations and territories taking part under their own flags.

subtopic: FIFA World Cup history and current editions
text: Where was the inaugural FIFA World Cup held in 1930?
explanation: The first FIFA World Cup was held in Uruguay in 1930, with all matches taking place in Montevideo.

subtopic: FIFA World Cup history and current editions
text: Which nation won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
explanation: Host nation Uruguay defeated Argentina 4–2 in the 1930 final and became the first FIFA World Cup champion.

subtopic: FIFA World Cup history and current editions
text: Which team won the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022 final?
explanation: Argentina defeated France on penalties after a 3–3 draw in the 2022 final at Lusail Stadium.

subtopic: FIFA World Cup history and current editions
text: Who received the Golden Ball as the best player of the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022?
explanation: Lionel Messi won the adidas Golden Ball at Qatar 2022, while Kylian Mbappé won the Golden Boot.

subtopic: FIFA World Cup history and current editions
text: What historic result did Morocco achieve at the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022?
options: First Asian team to reach the World Cup final
First African team to reach a World Cup semi-final
First Arab team to win the World Cup title
First African team to finish as World Cup runner-up
explanation: Morocco became the first African team to reach a FIFA World Cup semi-final, defeating Spain and Portugal before losing to France.

subtopic: FIFA World Cup history and current editions
text: Which countries jointly hosted the FIFA World Cup 2026?
explanation: The 2026 FIFA World Cup was jointly hosted by Canada, Mexico and the United States, the first edition staged across three countries.

subtopic: FIFA World Cup history and current editions
text: How many national teams competed in the FIFA World Cup 2026?
explanation: The 2026 tournament was the first FIFA World Cup with a 48-team field, expanded from the 32-team format used in Qatar 2022.

subtopic: FIFA World Cup history and current editions
text: Which countries were appointed the principal hosts of the FIFA World Cup 2030?
explanation: Spain, Morocco and Portugal were appointed the principal hosts of the 2030 FIFA World Cup. Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay will stage centenary celebration matches.

subtopic: FIFA World Cup history and current editions
text: In which countries will the three centenary celebration matches of the FIFA World Cup 2030 be played?
explanation: The 2030 centenary celebration matches will be played in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, including a celebration of Uruguay hosting the inaugural 1930 World Cup.

subtopic: FIFA World Cup history and current editions
text: Where was the FIFA World Cup 2026 final scheduled to be played?
explanation: FIFA scheduled the 2026 final for New York New Jersey. The tournament used 16 host cities across Canada, Mexico and the United States.

text: Where was the first World Athletics Championships held in 1983?
explanation: The inaugural World Athletics Championships took place in Helsinki, Finland, in 1983.

text: Which organisation conducts the World Athletics Championships?
explanation: World Athletics, the international governing body for athletics, organises the World Athletics Championships.

text: Since which edition have the World Athletics Championships generally been held every two years?
explanation: The championships were originally held at four-year intervals; the cycle became biennial after the 1991 Tokyo edition, with Stuttgart following in 1993.

text: The World Athletics Championships held in Tokyo in 2025 were which edition?
explanation: Tokyo 2025 was the 20th edition of the World Athletics Championships, held from 13 to 21 September 2025.

text: What were the dates of the World Athletics Championships Tokyo 2025?
explanation: The Tokyo 2025 championships were held from 13 to 21 September 2025 at the Japan National Stadium and other venues.

text: At the 1991 World Championships in Tokyo, whose legal long-jump mark of 8.95 m surpassed Bob Beamon's 1968 world record?
explanation: Mike Powell jumped 8.95 m in the fifth round at Tokyo 1991, exceeding Bob Beamon's 8.90 m world record from the 1968 Olympics.

text: Which performance did Usain Bolt record at the 2009 World Championships in Berlin?
explanation: At Berlin 2009, Usain Bolt set the 100 m world record at 9.58 seconds and also set a 200 m world record of 19.19 seconds.

text: Which pairing correctly identifies the combined events at the senior World Athletics Championships?
explanation: The senior outdoor programme includes the men's decathlon and the women's heptathlon as its two combined events.

text: At Budapest 2023, which athlete completed the men's 100 m and 200 m individual-title double?
explanation: Noah Lyles won both the men's 100 m and 200 m at the 2023 World Championships in Budapest, then added a 4×100 m relay gold.

text: Why were the World Athletics Championships scheduled for Eugene in 2021 held in 2022 instead?
options: A change in the athletics qualification rules
A cancellation of the World Athletics season
The Tokyo Olympic Games were postponed
explanation: The Eugene championships moved from 2021 to 2022 because the Tokyo Olympics had been rescheduled to 2021 after the COVID-19 disruption.

subtopic: Other major World Cups and World Championships
text: Where was the inaugural World Aquatics Championships held in 1973?
explanation: The first FINA World Championships, now known as the World Aquatics Championships, were held in Belgrade in 1973.

subtopic: Other major World Cups and World Championships
text: Which of the following is an official discipline at the World Aquatics Championships?
explanation: High diving is one of the six disciplines described by World Aquatics for its championships, alongside swimming, diving, water polo, artistic swimming and open water swimming.

subtopic: Other major World Cups and World Championships
text: Since which year have the World Aquatics Championships generally been staged in odd-numbered years on a biennial cycle?
explanation: World Aquatics records that the championships returned to a biennial, odd-numbered-year cycle from 2001, beginning with Fukuoka.

subtopic: Other major World Cups and World Championships
text: Which country hosted the World Aquatics Championships in 2025?
explanation: The World Aquatics Championships were held in Singapore in 2025. Doha hosted the 2024 edition and Fukuoka hosted the 2023 edition.

subtopic: Other major World Cups and World Championships
text: Which city is scheduled to host the World Aquatics Championships in 2027?
explanation: Budapest is scheduled to host the 2027 World Aquatics Championships, returning to the city that hosted editions in 2017 and 2022.

subtopic: Other major World Cups and World Championships
text: In which country was the first FIBA Basketball World Cup held in 1950?
explanation: The first FIBA Basketball World Cup took place in Argentina in 1950, and the host nation won the final against the United States.

subtopic: Other major World Cups and World Championships
text: Which country won the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023?
explanation: Germany won the 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup; Serbia finished second and Canada finished third.

subtopic: Other major World Cups and World Championships
text: Which city and country will host the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027?
explanation: The FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 will be hosted in Doha, Qatar, with all games planned for the same city.

subtopic: Other major World Cups and World Championships
text: How many national teams are scheduled for the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027?
explanation: FIBA's official information states that 32 national teams will compete at the 2027 World Cup in Qatar.

subtopic: Other major World Cups and World Championships
text: Under FIBA's current qualification framework, how many teams will qualify directly from the World Cup to the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic basketball tournament?
explanation: FIBA's current competition information states that seven national teams qualify directly from the 2027 World Cup, with the United States qualifying as host; the framework remains subject to the stated FIBA Central Board arrangements.

text: Which description best captures the aim of a safe sporting environment?
options: An environment focused only on winning and selection
An environment where athletes manage concerns without support
An environment where coaches decide all welfare matters privately
An environment free from harassment, abuse and discrimination
explanation: IOC safe-sport material treats safety, respect and protection from harassment, abuse and discrimination as fundamental conditions for participation.

text: In an athlete-safeguarding policy, which element most directly establishes accountability?
options: A list of preferred competition venues
A named policy owner responsible for implementation
A ranking system for national-team selection
A schedule for routine strength-training sessions
explanation: The IOC safeguarding toolkit recommends identifying who is responsible for implementing and upholding the safeguarding policy.

text: A physiotherapist notices repeated unexplained injuries in a young athlete who has become withdrawn. What is the most appropriate first safeguarding response?
options: Report the concern through the sport welfare officer
Wait for the athlete to make a formal complaint
Discuss the matter publicly so teammates can investigate
Ignore the pattern unless performance also declines
explanation: IOC safeguarding education advises reporting concerns about an athlete’s safety or well-being to the sport welfare or safeguarding officer rather than remaining silent.

text: Which approach is recommended when developing an organisation’s athlete-safeguarding policy?
options: Consult athletes and review the policy regularly
Keep the policy confidential so it cannot be challenged
Apply it only to athletes who are minors
Review it only after a serious incident has occurred
explanation: The IOC toolkit recommends developing policies in consultation with athletes and reviewing them regularly, especially after changes in law or organisational rules.

text: A high-performance centre is revising its athlete-welfare arrangements. Which priority is most consistent with SAI’s Athlete Wellbeing Policy published in 2026?
options: Protecting athlete safety, health and well-being in sport
Replacing welfare support with performance targets
Restricting welfare services to medal-winning athletes
Treating welfare concerns as outside sport administration
explanation: SAI’s Athlete Wellbeing Policy is an athlete-centred welfare measure; its purpose is to support safety, health and well-being in the sporting environment, not only competitive outcomes.

text: Before beginning a physiotherapy examination, which ethical safeguard should normally be obtained from the athlete?
options: Voluntary informed consent after relevant information
A promise that the athlete will follow every recommendation
Written approval from every member of the coaching staff
A guarantee that the examination will improve performance
explanation: World Physiotherapy’s informed-consent policy places the athlete’s voluntary, informed choice before examination and treatment, subject to applicable law and circumstances.

text: A volunteer repeatedly asks an athlete to meet alone in a hotel room and tells the athlete not to mention it. What is the safest response?
options: Raise the concern with a welfare or safeguarding officer
Accept because the volunteer is part of the team
Keep silent unless physical contact occurs
Ask teammates to decide if the conduct is acceptable
explanation: The IOC’s safeguarding scenarios identify secretive one-to-one approaches that make an athlete uncomfortable as concerns to raise with a welfare or safeguarding officer.

text: Why should an athlete-safeguarding policy include a third-party reporting or whistleblowing route?
options: A safe route when internal reporting is unavailable
To replace all internal disciplinary procedures
To allow anonymous selection of teams without review
To publish allegations before an inquiry begins
explanation: The IOC safeguarding toolkit recommends guidance for third-party reporting so that concerns can still be raised when an internal route is unavailable or unsafe.

text: An athlete reports discriminatory comments from teammates. Which response best reflects safe-sport practice?
options: Advise the athlete to tolerate the comments as part of team culture
Take the concern seriously, protect the athlete and report it
Move the athlete to another group without recording the concern
Wait until several athletes submit identical complaints
explanation: IOC safe-sport guidance treats discrimination and harassment as unacceptable and supports respectful environments, reporting, and access to protection and support.

text: Which professional value should guide a physiotherapist’s interaction with an athlete who discloses a welfare concern?
options: Priority to the coach’s convenience over the athlete’s account
Disclosure of the account to the whole training group
Respect for dignity, autonomy, confidentiality and welfare
Continuation of treatment without explaining available choices
explanation: World Physiotherapy’s ethical principles emphasise respect for dignity, autonomy, privacy, confidentiality and the welfare of people receiving physiotherapy.

text: The POSH law referred to in Indian workplace-safeguarding guidance is formally known as which Act?
options: Sexual Harassment of Employees at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2014
Sexual Harassment of Women in Employment (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2012
Sexual Harassment of Workers at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2015
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
explanation: India Code identifies the governing statute as the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.

text: Under the POSH Act, which person can fall within the definition of an aggrieved woman at a workplace?
options: Only a permanent employee with a written contract
Only a woman employed for one complete year
A woman of any age, employed or not, alleging harassment
Only a woman selected for a national sports team
explanation: Section 2 of the POSH Act defines an aggrieved woman at a workplace as a woman of any age, whether employed or not, who alleges sexual harassment.

text: Under Section 4 of the POSH Act, who should preside over an Internal Committee where practicable?
options: The most senior male coach in the organisation
An external lawyer chosen by the respondent
The district officer responsible for local committees
A senior woman employee of the organisation
explanation: Section 4 provides that the Presiding Officer of the Internal Committee shall be a senior-level woman employee, where available.

text: What is the usual time limit for submitting a written complaint under Section 9 of the POSH Act?
options: Thirty calendar days from the alleged workplace incident
Six calendar months after the sports season ends
Three months from the incident or last incident in a series
One year from the incident, regardless of series
explanation: Section 9 generally allows a written complaint within three months of the incident, or the last incident in a series; the committee may extend this by up to a further three months for recorded reasons.

text: During POSH conciliation, which condition is expressly prohibited as the basis of settlement?
options: A written record of the agreed non-monetary measures
A monetary settlement as the basis of conciliation
A request that the parties receive information about the process
A voluntary request for conciliation made by the aggrieved woman
explanation: Section 10 permits conciliation at the request of the aggrieved woman but states that monetary settlement shall not be made as its basis.

text: Within what period should an inquiry under Section 11 of the POSH Act ordinarily be completed?
explanation: Section 11 states that an inquiry should be completed within ninety days.

text: After completing a POSH inquiry, within what period should the committee provide its report to the employer or District Officer?
options: Within thirty days of receiving the complaint
Within sixty days of constituting the committee
Within ten days of completing the inquiry
Within ninety days of the first hearing
explanation: Section 13 requires the Internal Committee or Local Committee to provide its findings report within ten days of completing the inquiry.

text: A staff member shares the names and allegations from a POSH inquiry in a team messaging group. Which principle has most clearly been breached?
options: The rule requiring conciliation before every inquiry
The requirement to transfer every respondent
The rule that only athletes may submit complaints
Confidentiality for complaint and inquiry details
explanation: Section 16 prohibits publication or making known the contents of a complaint, the identities of the parties and witnesses, and related conciliation or inquiry information.

text: While a POSH inquiry is pending, what temporary relief may be recommended on a written request from the aggrieved woman?
options: Permanent cancellation of the professional licence
Transfer or up to three months' leave for her
Publication of allegations on the public website
explanation: Section 12 permits recommendations such as transfer or leave for the aggrieved woman; the leave may be up to three months in addition to ordinary leave.

text: Which action is a duty of an employer under the POSH Act?
options: Decide every complaint without a committee
Publish identities to deter future complaints
Provide awareness measures and display consequences
explanation: Section 19 includes prevention duties such as providing a safe working environment, displaying penal consequences, and organising awareness and sensitisation programmes.

text: A physiotherapist is asked to assess an athlete from a team owned by the physiotherapist’s close relative. What is the most ethical action?
options: Proceed without disclosure because clinical tests are objective
Disclose the conflict and request an impartial assessor
Ask the relative to approve the assessment after it is completed
Change the results so the conflict cannot be detected
explanation: A close relationship creates a potential conflict of interest. Transparency and independent assessment protect the athlete and the integrity of the decision.

text: Which statement best reflects informed consent in sports physiotherapy?
options: Consent is implied by entering a training centre
A coach can consent for every adult athlete
Consent is unnecessary for performance treatment
explanation: World Physiotherapy describes informed consent as a voluntary choice made after relevant information is communicated in a way the person can understand.

text: An athlete’s medical information should ordinarily be shared with which group?
options: Anyone who follows the athlete or attends competitions
Only authorised people with a legitimate need to know
All spectators who ask about an absence
Every athlete in the same training squad
explanation: Confidentiality and privacy require limiting disclosure to authorised people with a legitimate role and need to know, subject to consent and applicable law.

text: Which practice most clearly reflects evidence-informed professional conduct?
options: Using a popular intervention for every athlete regardless of need
Selecting treatment solely because a sponsor promotes it
Withholding uncertainty so the athlete cannot question a plan
Combining evidence, expertise and athlete preferences
explanation: Evidence-informed practice integrates the best available evidence with professional judgement and the individual athlete’s values, preferences and circumstances.

text: A coach asks a performance analyst to conceal a rule violation by an opponent. Which response best represents fair play?
options: Conceal it if the team is unlikely to be caught
Refuse concealment and use the proper reporting route
Post an allegation online before checking facts
Ignore it because staff cannot affect fair play
explanation: Fair play requires respect for rules and honest conduct by everyone involved in sport; concerns should be handled through an appropriate process.

text: Which selection practice is most consistent with ethical and inclusive sports administration?
options: Use an undisclosed personal preference as the only criterion
Apply transparent, relevant criteria without discrimination
Give preference to athletes who provide private benefits to staff
Exclude an athlete after rumours without an opportunity to respond
explanation: Ethical governance requires fair, relevant and transparent decision-making and rejects discrimination, favouritism and decisions based on unverified personal interests.

text: A staff member pressures a physiotherapist to remove an unfavourable finding from an injury report. What should the physiotherapist do?
options: Remove it if the athlete wants to compete without review
Replace it with a less serious diagnosis without retesting
Keep the accurate record and escalate improper pressure
Delete it and rely on an undocumented verbal handover
explanation: Accurate documentation and professional integrity take priority over selection pressure. An attempt to alter a clinical record should be documented and reported through an appropriate channel.

text: What is the most appropriate data-governance principle when collecting athlete monitoring information?
options: Collect every available variable because storage has no ethical cost
Retain identifiable data permanently even when no purpose remains
Use relevant data for a defined purpose with protection
Give unrestricted access to all staff so decisions are faster
explanation: Responsible athlete-data governance emphasises a defined purpose, appropriate collection and access, protection of information, and accountable use.

text: A senior staff member asks an athlete to keep a personal relationship secret in exchange for selection support. Which ethical concern is primary?
options: Abuse of power and a breach of professional boundaries
A harmless arrangement because selection is always subjective
A normal performance incentive that requires no disclosure
A scheduling issue that should be handled only by the coach
explanation: A person controlling selection has power over the athlete. Linking that power to a secret personal relationship creates coercive pressure and violates professional boundaries and safe-sport principles.

text: Which statement best describes fair play in sport?
options: Respecting rules, opponents, officials and fair competition
Winning permits bending a rule when officials do not notice
Following rules only during televised competitions
Allowing the strongest team to decide which rules apply
explanation: Fair play combines compliance with rules and respect for opponents, officials and the spirit of sport; it is not conditional on being observed.

text: Which title identifies the Indian statute enacted in 2025 to address sports governance, welfare and ethical practices?
explanation: The official Gazette text published in 2025 is titled the National Sports Governance Act, 2025. Its commencement is by notification under Section 1(2).

text: Under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, which set lists the national sports governing bodies named for recognised organisations?
options: NOC and Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports only
National Sports Federations and State Sports Departments only
NOC, National Sports Federations and private leagues
NOC, NPC, National and Regional Sports Federations
explanation: Section 3 names the National Olympic Committee, National Paralympic Committee, National Sports Federations for designated sports and Regional Sports Federations as national sports governing bodies.

text: Who is covered by the Code of Ethics required of every National Sports Body under Section 12 of the 2025 Act?
options: Committees, staff, sponsors, coaches, athletes, officials and others
Only the president and secretary of the National Sports Body
Only athletes registered internationally and accredited team staff
Only government employees assigned to sports administration
explanation: Section 12 applies the Code of Ethics to executive and other committees, employees, staff, sponsors, coaches, athletes, officials, members, affiliates and other relevant persons.

text: Under Section 12 of the National Sports Governance Act, which person is in a position of trust?
options: Has won an Olympic or Asian Games medal in any discipline
Has served five years as a sports journalist in a recognised federation
Holds a paid role in any recognised private fitness organisation
Exercises authority or influence over another person or dependent
explanation: The Act defines a person in a position of trust by authority, control or influence over another person, or by the other person’s dependence on them in connection with the sports body.

text: A National Sports Body is planning an event, training camp and disciplinary hearing. Under the 2025 Act’s Safe Sports Policy provision, which activities should be covered?
options: All National Sports Body activities, events and proceedings
Only the final competition, medal ceremony and official media activities
Only activities involving women athletes at the event and camp
Only activities conducted outside India during official tours
explanation: Section 13 requires a comprehensive Safe Sports Policy applicable to all activities, events, operations and proceedings conducted by National Sports Bodies.

text: What standard should an internal grievance-redressal mechanism of a National Sports Body meet under Section 13?
options: It should be confidential but need not give reasons
It should address grievances fairly, promptly and transparently
It should be controlled only by the accused person
It should decide matters only after the next election
explanation: Section 13 requires an internal grievance-redressal mechanism for athletes, coaches and others associated with the body, operating in a fair, timely and transparent manner.

text: Under Section 14 of the National Sports Governance Act, which organisation is eligible to receive grants or other financial assistance from the Central Government?
options: Any informal group claiming to promote a sport
Only a commercial league with private investors
A sports organisation recognised under the Act
Only an organisation that has hosted an Olympic Games
explanation: Section 14(1) states that only a recognised sports organisation is eligible to receive grants or other financial assistance from the Central Government.

text: A recognised sports organisation receives a government grant. For what purpose does it have public-authority status under Section 14(2)?
options: For every private contract by athletes and staff
Only for determining a competition result
Only for regulating international sport rules
For use of the government grant or other assistance
explanation: Section 14(2) treats a recognised sports organisation receiving government financial assistance as a public authority under the Right to Information Act with respect to utilisation of that assistance.

text: Under Section 17 of the National Sports Governance Act, which qualification is specified for the Chairperson of the National Sports Tribunal?
options: Former international athlete with five years' service
Serving secretary of a recognised National Sports Federation
Retired coach nominated by the National Olympic Committee
Present or former Supreme Court Judge or High Court Chief Justice
explanation: Section 17(2) specifies that the Tribunal Chairperson shall be a person who is or has been a Judge of the Supreme Court or the Chief Justice of a High Court.

text: Which persons are intended to form the National Sports Election Panel under Section 16 of the 2025 Act?
options: Serving coaches selected by the National Olympic Committee
Retired election officials with relevant experience
Athletes elected by each National Sports Federation
Representatives of sponsors who fund national teams
explanation: Section 16 provides for a panel of retired Chief Election Commissioners, Election Commissioners, Deputy Election Commissioners, State Election Commissioners or Chief Electoral Officers with relevant election experience.
